The oracle checks that lastTx[attacker_address] > 0, which can be achieved by making a transfer while in Restricted mode. We need to: 1) Switch contract to Restricted mode (requires owner), 2) Get tokens to transfer, 3) Make a transfer to trigger lastTx update.
attack_strategy: Impersonate owner to enable Restricted mode, then perform a transfer to set lastTx[attacker] > 0.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Find owner address via owner() function. 2. Impersonate owner with vm.prank(). 3. Call setBotProtection(true) to enable Restricted mode. 4. Transfer some tokens from owner to attacker. 5. As attacker, transfer tokens to another address to trigger lastTx update. 6. Verify lastTx[attacker] > 0.

vulnerability_analysis: The oracle checks lastTx[attacker_address] > 0. This can be achieved in either Restricted mode (sets lastTx for all transfers) or Unlocked mode (sets lastTx only for blacklisted addresses). Since contract is already Unlocked, we need to get blacklisted and then make a transfer.
attack_strategy: 1. As owner, blacklist the attacker address. 2. As attacker, make a transfer (which will set lastTx[attacker] in Unlocked mode for blacklisted addresses).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate owner. 2. Call blacklistAccount(attacker, true). 3. Ensure attacker has tokens. 4. As attacker, transfer tokens to trigger lastTx update for blacklisted sender.
failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because the contract was already in Unlocked state (2), and setBotProtection(true) only switches to Restricted if the current state is Locked (0). We can't go from Unlocked to Restricted directly. Need alternative approach.
